faq.a: If you want one journal that does it all, yes. Auserene connects quick notes, an evening conversation, a meditation made from your day, memory you can read and edit, people and habit goals, with no ads and a free plan you can keep. Mindsera is the better pick for frameworks, emotion analysis, live voice calls, or if you need Android, Wear OS or the web.

Mindsera has a free Curious plan with the journal, habit tracker, frameworks and export. AI features, including memory, voice journaling and Call Mode, need Genius, though free members can try most of them once or a few times. Auserene's free plan has no time limit and covers notes, scanning, mood, journeys, goals and people.

As of November 19, 2026, Mindsera Genius costs $14.99 a month or $129 a year on its website. Its App Store listing also shows a $99 annual offer and a $17.99 monthly offer. Students, people over 65 and people with disabilities can ask for 40% off. Auserene Premium is $11.99 a month or $105.99 a year.

Yes, on Genius. Its Memory Profile is a set of summaries built from your entries and refreshed each night, and Mindsera says you can view, edit, delete or switch it off. Auserene's You tab works the same way, and its memory also reaches each person's page, your meditation and your habit goals.

Mindsera doesn't list a meditation or breathing feature on its site, help center or App Store listing. Auserene writes a guided meditation from each day's conversation, has eight guided meditation journeys and 11 ambient sounds, and does haptic breathing on Apple Watch.

faq.q: What is a good Mindsera alternative for iPhone?
faq.a: Auserene, if you want your notes, conversation, meditation, memory, people and goals in one connected app on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. Rosebud, if you want guided, therapy-informed journals and don't mind paying from day one. Apple Journal, if you want something free and end-to-end encrypted with no AI chat.
